readings.title: Nebuchadnezzar's Troubling Dream
readings.subtitle: Daniel Seeks Divine Revelation
readings.text:
[Daniel 2:1] And in the second year of the reign of Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar, Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar had dreams. And his spirit was so troubled that his sleep left him.
[2] And the sovereign gave orders to call the magicians, and the astrologers, and the practisers of witchcraft, and the Kasdim to declare to the sovereign his dreams. So they came and stood before the sovereign.
[3] And the sovereign said to them, “<dn>I</dn> have had a dream, and <dn>my</dn> spirit is troubled to know the dream.”
[4] And the Kasdim spoke to the sovereign in Aramaic, “O sovereign, live forever! Relate the dream to your servants, and we shall reveal the interpretation.”
[5] The sovereign answered and said to the Kasdim, “<dn>My</dn> decision is firm: if you do not make known the dream and its interpretation to me, your limbs shall be taken from you, and your houses made dunghills.
[6] “But if you reveal the dream and its interpretation, you shall receive gifts, and rewards, and great esteem from me. So reveal to me the dream and its interpretation.”
[7] They answered again and said, “Let the sovereign relate to his servants the dream, and we shall reveal its interpretation.”
[8] The sovereign answered and said, “<dn>I</dn> know for certain that you would gain time, because you see that <dn>my</dn> decision is firm:
[9] “If you do not make known the dream to me, there is only one decree for you! For you have agreed to speak lying and corrupt words before me till the time has changed. So relate the dream to me, then <dn>I</dn> shall know that you shall reveal its interpretation for me.”
[10] The Kasdim answered the sovereign, and said, “There is no one on earth who is able to reveal the matter of the sovereign. Because no sovereign, master, or ruler has ever asked a matter like this of any magician, or astrologer, or Kasdim.
[11] “And the matter that the sovereign is asking is difficult, and there is no other who is able to reveal it to the sovereign except the elahin, whose dwelling is not with flesh.”
[12] Because of this the sovereign was enraged and very wroth, and gave orders to destroy all the wise ones of Baḇel.
[13] So the decree went out, and they began killing· the wise ones. And they sought <dn>את</dn> Dani’ěl and his companions, to kill· them.
[14] Then with counsel and wisdom Dani’ěl answered Aryoḵ, the chief of the sovereign’s guard, who had gone out to kill· the wise ones of Baḇel –
[15] he answered and said to Aryoḵ the sovereign’s officer, “Why is the decree from the sovereign so urgent?” So Aryoḵ made <dn>את</dn> the decision known to Dani’ěl.
[16] And Dani’ěl went in and asked the sovereign to give him time, and he would show the sovereign the interpretation.
[17] Then Dani’ěl went to his house, and made <dn>את</dn> the decision known to Ḥananyah, Misha’ěl, and Azaryah, his companions,
[18] to seek compassion from the <dn>Elah</dn> of the heavens concerning this secret, so that Dani’ěl and his companions should not perish with the rest of the wise ones of Baḇel.
[19] Then <dn>את</dn> the secret was revealed to Dani’ěl in a night vision, and Dani’ěl blessed the <dn>Elah</dn> of the heavens.
[20] Dani’ěl responded and said, <dq>“Blessed be the Name of <dn>Elah</dn> forever and ever, for wisdom and might are <dn>His</dn>.</dq>
[21] <dq>“And <dn>He</dn> changes the times and the seasons. <dn>He</dn> removes sovereigns and raises up sovereigns. <dn>He</dn> gives wisdom to the wise and knowledge to those who possess understanding.</dq>
[22] <dq>“<dn>He</dn> reveals deep and secret matters. <dn>He</dn> knows what is in the darkness, and light dwells with <dn>Him</dn>.</dq>
[23] <dq>“<dn>I</dn> thank <dn>You</dn> and praise <dn>You</dn>, O <dn>Elah</dn> of my fathers. <dn>You</dn> have given me wisdom and might, and have now made known to me <dn>את</dn> what we asked of <dn>You</dn>, for <dn>You</dn> have made known to us <dn>את</dn> the sovereign’s matter.”</dq>

readings.title: The Great Image of Four Kingdoms
readings.subtitle: Daniel Reveals the Dream and its Meaning
readings.text:
[Daniel 2:24] So Dani’ěl went to Aryoḵ, whom the sovereign had appointed to destroy the wise ones of Baḇel. He went and said this to him, “Do not destroy the wise ones of Baḇel. Bring me in before the sovereign, and <dn>I</dn> shall show the interpretation to the sovereign.”
[25] Then Aryoḵ brought Dani’ěl in a hurry before the sovereign, and said thus to him, “<dn>I</dn> have found a man among the sons of the exile of Yehuḏah, who does make known to the sovereign the interpretation.”
[26] The sovereign answered and said to Dani’ěl, whose name was Bělteshatstsar, “Are you able to make known to me the dream which <dn>I</dn> have seen, and its interpretation?”
[27] Dani’ěl answered before the sovereign, and said, “The secret which the sovereign is asking – the wise ones, the astrologers, the magicians, and the diviners are unable to show it to the sovereign.
[28] <dq>“But there is an <dn>Elah</dn> in the heavens who reveals secrets, and <dn>He</dn> has made known to Sovereign Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar <dn>את</dn> what is to be in the latter days. Your dream, and the visions of your head upon your bed, were these:</dq>
[29] <dq>“As for you, O sovereign, on your bed your thoughts came up: What is going to take place after this. And <dn>He</dn> who reveals secrets has made known to you <dn>את</dn> what shall be after this.</dq>
[30] <dq>“As for me, this secret has not been revealed to me because <dn>I</dn> have more wisdom than anyone living, but for our sakes who make known the interpretation to the sovereign, and that you should know <dn>את</dn> the thoughts of your heart.</dq>
[31] <dq>“You, O sovereign, were looking on, and saw a great image! This great image, and its brightness excellent, was standing before you, and its form was awesome.</dq>
[32] <dq>“This image’s head was of fine gold, its chest and arms of silver, its belly and thighs of bronze,</dq>
[33] <dq>its legs of iron, its feet partly of iron and partly of clay.</dq>
[34] <dq>“You were looking on, until a stone was cut out without hands, and it smote <dn>את</dn> the image on its feet of iron and clay, and broke them in pieces.</dq>
[35] <dq>“Then the iron, the clay, the bronze, the silver, and the gold were crushed together, and became like chaff from the summer threshing-floors. And the wind took them away so that no trace of them was found. And the stone that smote <dn>את</dn> the image became a great mountain and filled <dn>את</dn> all the earth.</dq>
[36] <dq>“This is the dream, and its interpretation we declare before the sovereign.</dq>
[37] <dq>“You, O sovereign, are a sovereign of sovereigns. For the <dn>Elah</dn> of the heavens has given you a reign, power, and strength, and preciousness,</dq>
[38] <dq>and wherever the children of men dwell, or the beasts of the field and the birds of the heavens, <dn>He</dn> has given them into your hand, and has made you ruler over them all. You are the head of gold.</dq>
[39] <dq>“And after you rises up another reign lower than yours, and another third reign of bronze that rules over all the earth.</dq>
[40] <dq>“And the fourth reign is as strong as iron, because iron crushes and shatters all. So, like iron that breaks in pieces, it crushes and breaks all these.</dq>
[41] <dq>“Yet, as you saw the feet and toes, partly of potter’s clay and partly of iron, the reign is to be divided. But some of the strength of the iron is to be in it, because you saw the iron mixed with muddy clay.</dq>
[42] <dq>“And as the toes of the feet were partly of iron and partly of clay, so the reign is partly strong and partly brittle.</dq>
[43] <dq>“And as you saw iron mixed with muddy clay, they are mixing themselves with the seed of men, but they are not clinging to each other, even as iron does not mix with clay.</dq>
[44] <dq>“And in the days of these sovereigns the <dn>Elah</dn> of the heavens shall set up a reign which shall never be destroyed, nor the reign pass on to other people – it crushes and puts to an end <dn>את</dn> all these reigns, and it shall stand forever.</dq>
[45] <dq>“Because you saw that the stone was cut out of the mountain without hands, and that it crushed <dn>את</dn> the iron, <dn>את</dn> the bronze, <dn>את</dn> the clay, <dn>את</dn> the silver, and <dn>את</dn> the gold, the great <dn>Elah</dn> has made known to the sovereign <dn>את</dn> what shall be after this. And the dream is true, and its interpretation is trustworthy.”</dq>

readings.title: The King's Acknowledgment
readings.subtitle: Daniel and His Companions are Promoted
readings.text:
[Daniel 2:46] Then Sovereign Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar fell on his face, and did obeisance before Dani’ěl, and gave orders to present to him an offering and incense.
[47] The sovereign answered Dani’ěl, and said, “Truly your <dn>Elah</dn> is the <dn>Elah</dn> of elahin, the Master of sovereigns, and a revealer of secrets, since you were able to reveal this secret.”
[48] Then the sovereign made Dani’ěl great and gave him many great gifts, and made him ruler over all the province of Baḇel, and chief of the nobles, over all the wise ones of Baḇel.
[49] And Dani’ěl asked of the sovereign, and he set <dn>את</dn> Shaḏraḵ, <dn>את</dn> Měyshaḵ, and <dn>את</dn> Aḇěḏ-Neḡo over the work of the province of Baḇel, and Dani’ěl in the gate of the sovereign.

readings.title: The Golden Image
readings.subtitle: Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-Nego Refuse to Bow
readings.text:
[Daniel 3:1] Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar the sovereign made <dn>את</dn> an image of gold, whose height was sixty cubits and its width six cubits. He set it up in the plain of Dura, in the province of Baḇel.
[2] And Sovereign Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar sent word to gather together the viceroys, the nobles, and the governors, the counsellors, the treasurers, the judges, the magistrates, and all the officials of the provinces, to come to the dedication of the image which Sovereign Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar had set up.
[3] Then the viceroys, the nobles, and the governors, the counsellors, the treasurers, the judges, the magistrates, and all the officials of the provinces gathered together for the dedication of the image that Sovereign Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar had set up. And they stood before the image that Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar had set up.
[4] Then a herald loudly proclaimed, “To you it is commanded, O peoples, nations, and languages,
[5] that as soon as you hear the sound of the horn, the flute, the zither, the lyre, the harp, the pipes, and all kinds of instruments, you shall fall down and do obeisance to the gold image that Sovereign Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar has set up.
[6] “And whoever does not fall down and do obeisance is immediately thrown into the midst of a burning furnace of fire.”
[7] So as soon as all the people heard the sound of the horn, the flute, the zither, the lyre, the harp, all kinds of instruments, all the people, nations, and languages fell down and did obeisance to the gold image that Sovereign Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar had set up.
[8] Thereupon, at that time, certain Kasdim came forward and accused the Yehuḏim.
[9] They spoke and said to Sovereign Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar, “O sovereign, live forever!
[10] “You, O sovereign, have made a decree that everyone who hears the sound of the horn, the flute, the zither, the lyre, the harp, the pipes, and all kinds of instruments, shall fall down and do obeisance to the gold image,
[11] and whoever does not fall down and do obeisance is thrown into the midst of a burning furnace of fire.
[12] “There are certain Yehuḏim whom you have set over the work of the province of Baḇel: Shaḏraḵ, Měyshaḵ, and Aḇěḏ-Neḡo. These men, O sovereign, pay no heed to you. They do not serve <dn>את</dn> your elahin, and they are not doing obeisance to the gold image which you have set up.”
[13] Then Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar, in rage and wrath, gave orders to bring Shaḏraḵ, Měyshaḵ, and Aḇěḏ-Neḡo. Then they brought these men before the sovereign.
[14] Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar spoke and said to them, “Is it true, Shaḏraḵ, Měyshaḵ, and Aḇěḏ-Neḡo, that you do not serve <dn>את</dn> my elahin, and you do not do obeisance to the gold image which <dn>I</dn> have set up?
[15] “Now if you are ready when you hear the sound of the horn, the flute, the zither, the lyre, the harp, the pipes, and all kinds of instruments, and you fall down and do obeisance to the image which <dn>I</dn> have made, good! But if you do not do obeisance, you are immediately thrown into the midst of a burning furnace of fire. And who is the elah who does deliver you from my hands?”
[16] Shaḏraḵ, Měyshaḵ, and Aḇěḏ-Neḡo answered and said to the sovereign, “O Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar, we have no need to answer you in this matter.
[17] <dq>“For if so, our <dn>Elah</dn> whom we serve is able to deliver us from the burning furnace of fire and from your hand, O sovereign – <dn>He</dn> does deliver!</dq>
[18] <dq>“But if not, let it be known to you, O sovereign, that we do not serve your elahin, nor do we do obeisance to the gold image which you have set up.”</dq>

readings.title: The Fiery Furnace
readings.subtitle: Deliverance and the King's Decree
readings.text:
[Daniel 3:19] Then Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar was filled with wrath, and the expression on his face changed toward Shaḏraḵ, Měyshaḵ, and Aḇěḏ-Neḡo. He responded and gave orders that they heat the furnace seven times more than it was usual to heat it.
[20] And he commanded some of the strongest men of his army to bind <dn>את</dn> Shaḏraḵ, <dn>את</dn> Měyshaḵ, and <dn>את</dn> Aḇěḏ-Neḡo, and throw them into the burning furnace of fire.
[21] So these men were bound in their coats, their trousers, and their turbans, and their other garments, and were thrown into the midst of the burning furnace of fire.
[22] Thereupon, because the sovereign’s order was urgent, and the furnace exceedingly hot, the flame of the fire killed· <dn>את</dn> those men who took up <dn>את</dn> Shaḏraḵ, <dn>את</dn> Měyshaḵ, and <dn>את</dn> Aḇěḏ-Neḡo.
[23] And these three men, Shaḏraḵ, Měyshaḵ, and Aḇěḏ-Neḡo, fell down bound into the midst of the burning furnace of fire.
[24] Then Sovereign Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar was amazed, and stood up in haste and spoke and said to his counsellors, “Did we not throw three men bound into the midst of the fire?” They answered and said to the sovereign, “Certainly, O sovereign.”
[25] He answered and said, “Look! <dn>I</dn> see four men loose, walking in the midst of the fire. And they are not hurt, and the form of the fourth is like the Son of <dn>Elahin</dn>.”
[26] Then Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar went near the mouth of the burning furnace of fire. He spoke and said, “Shaḏraḵ, Měyshaḵ, and Aḇěḏ-Neḡo, servants of the Most High <dn>Elah</dn>, come out, and come here.” Then Shaḏraḵ, Měyshaḵ, and Aḇěḏ-Neḡo came from the midst of the fire.
[27] And the viceroys, the nobles, and the governors, and the sovereign’s counsellors gathered together, seeing these men on whose bodies the fire had no power, and the hair of their head was not singed nor were their garments changed, nor did the smell of fire come on them.
[28] Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar responded and said, <dq>“Blessed be the <dn>Elah</dn> of Shaḏraḵ, Měyshaḵ, and Aḇěḏ-Neḡo, who sent <dn>His</dn> Messenger and delivered <dn>His</dn> servants who trusted in <dn>Him</dn>, and changed <dn>את</dn> the sovereign’s order, and gave up their bodies, that they should not serve nor do obeisance to any elah except their own <dn>Elah</dn>!</dq>
[29] <dq>“Therefore <dn>I</dn> make a decree that whoever of any people, nation, or language who speaks any wrong against the <dn>Elah</dn> of Shaḏraḵ, Měyshaḵ, and Aḇěḏ-Neḡo, his limbs shall be taken, and his house made a dunghill, because there is no other <dn>Elah</dn> who is able to deliver like this.”</dq>
[30] Then the sovereign promoted <dn>את</dn> Shaḏraḵ, <dn>את</dn> Měyshaḵ, and <dn>את</dn> Aḇěḏ-Neḡo in the province of Baḇel.

readings.title: The Temple Sermon
readings.subtitle: False Trust in the House of YeHoVaH
readings.text:
[Jeremiah 7:1] The word that came to Yirmeyahu from <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, saying,
[2] <dq>“Stand in the gate of the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and you shall proclaim there <dn>את</dn> this word, and shall say, ‘Hear <dn>את</dn> the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, all you of Yehuḏah who enter in at these gates to bow before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>!’ ”</dq>
[3] <dq>Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, “Make your ways and your deeds good, then <dn>I</dn> let you dwell in this place.</dq>
[4] <dq>“Do not trust in these false words, saying, ‘This is the Hěḵal of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, the Hěḵal of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, the Hěḵal of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>!’</dq>
[5] <dq>“For if you truly make your ways and your deeds good, if you truly do right-ruling between a man and his neighbour,</dq>
[6] <dq>if you do not oppress <dn>את</dn> the stranger, <dn>את</dn> the fatherless, and <dn>את</dn> the widow, and do not shed innocent blood in this place, or walk after other mighty ones to your own evil,</dq>
[7] <dq>then <dn>I</dn> shall let you dwell in this place, in the land that <dn>I</dn> gave to your fathers forever and ever.</dq>
[8] <dq>“See, you are trusting in false words, which do not profit –</dq>
[9] <dq>stealing, murdering, and committing adultery, and swearing falsely, and burning incense to Ba‛al, and walking after other mighty ones you have not known.</dq>
[10] <dq>“And you came and stood before <dn>Me</dn> in this house which is called by <dn>My</dn> Name, and said, ‘We have been delivered’ – in order to do all these abominations!</dq>
[11] <dq>“Has this house, which is called by <dn>My</dn> Name, become a den of robbers in your eyes? Look, <dn>I</dn>, even <dn>I</dn> Myself have seen it,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.
[12] <dq>“But go now to <dn>My</dn> place at Shiloh, where <dn>I</dn> set <dn>My</dn> Name at the first, and see <dn>את</dn> what <dn>I</dn> did to it because of the evil of <dn>My</dn> people Yisra’ěl.</dq>
[13] <dq>“And now, because you have done all these works,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“and <dn>I</dn> spoke to you, rising up early and speaking, but you did not hear, and <dn>I</dn> called you, but you did not answer,</dq>
[14] <dq>“<dn>I</dn> shall also do to this house, which is called by <dn>My</dn> Name, in which you trust, and to this place which <dn>I</dn> gave to you and your fathers, as <dn>I</dn> did to Shiloh.</dq>
[15] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall cast you out of <dn>My</dn> presence, as <dn>I</dn> have cast out <dn>את</dn> all your brothers, <dn>את</dn> all the seed of Ephrayim.</dq>

readings.title: A People Beyond Intercession
readings.subtitle: The Worship of the Queen of Heaven
readings.text:
[Jeremiah 7:16] <dq>“And you, do not pray for this people, nor lift up a cry or prayer for them, nor make intercession to <dn>Me</dn>, for <dn>I</dn> do not hear you.</dq>
[17] <dq>“Do you not see <dn>את</dn> what they are doing in the cities of Yehuḏah and in the streets of Yerushalayim?</dq>
[18] <dq>“The children are gathering wood, the fathers are lighting the fire, and the women are kneading their dough, to make cakes for the sovereigness of the heavens, and to pour out drink offerings to other mighty ones, to provoke <dn>Me</dn>.</dq>
[19] <dq>“Is it <dn>Me</dn> they are provoking?”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. <dq>“Is it not themselves – unto the shame of their own faces?”</dq>
[20] Therefore, thus said the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“See, <dn>My</dn> displeasure and <dn>My</dn> wrath is poured out on this place, on man and on beast, and on the trees of the field and on the fruit of the ground. And it shall burn and not be quenched.”</dq>
[21] Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, <dq>“Add your ascending offerings to your slaughterings and eat meat.</dq>
[22] <dq>“For <dn>I</dn> did not speak to your fathers, or command them in the day that <dn>I</dn> brought them out of the land of Mitsrayim, about matters of ascending offerings or slaughterings.</dq>
[23] <dq>“But <dn>את</dn> this word <dn>I</dn> did command them, saying, ‘Obey <dn>My</dn> voice, and <dn>I</dn> shall be your <dn>Elohim</dn>, and you be <dn>My</dn> people. And walk in all the ways that <dn>I</dn> have commanded you, so that it be well with you.’</dq>
[24] <dq>“But they did not obey or incline their ear, but walked in the counsels, in the stubbornness of their evil heart, and went backward and not forward.</dq>
[25] <dq>“From the day that your fathers came out of the land of Mitsrayim until this day, <dn>I</dn> have even sent to you <dn>את</dn> all <dn>My</dn> servants the prophets, daily rising up early and sending them.</dq>
[26] <dq>“But they did not obey <dn>Me</dn> or incline their ear, but stiffened their neck. They did evil, more than their fathers.</dq>
[27] <dq>“And you shall speak <dn>את</dn> all these words to them, though they do not listen to you. And you shall also call to them, though they do not answer you.</dq>
[28] <dq>“But you shall say to them, ‘This is a nation that did not obey the voice of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> their <dn>Elohim</dn>, nor did they accept instruction. Truth has perished and has been cut off from their mouth.</dq>
[29] <dq>Cut off your hair and throw it away, and take up a lamentation on the bare heights, for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has rejected and forsaken <dn>את</dn> the generation of <dn>His</dn> wrath.’</dq>

readings.title: The Valley of Slaughter
readings.subtitle: Abominations and Desecration
readings.text:
[Jeremiah 7:30] <dq>“For the children of Yehuḏah have done what is evil in <dn>My</dn> eyes,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. <dq>“They have set their abominations in the house which is called by <dn>My</dn> Name, to defile it.</dq>
[31] <dq>“And they have built the high places of Topheth, which is in the Valley of the Son of Hinnom, to burn their sons and their daughters in the fire, which <dn>I</dn> did not command, nor did it come into <dn>My</dn> heart.</dq>
[32] <dq>“Therefore see, the days are coming,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“when it shall no longer be called Topheth, or the Valley of the Son of Hinnom, but the Valley of Slaughter, for they shall bury in Topheth until no room is left.</dq>
[33] <dq>“And the corpses of this people shall be food for the birds of the heavens and for the beasts of the earth, with none to frighten them away.</dq>
[34] <dq>“And in the cities of Yehuḏah and in the streets of Yerushalayim <dn>I</dn> shall make to cease <dn>את</dn> the voice of rejoicing and <dn>את</dn> the voice of gladness, <dn>את</dn> the voice of the bridegroom and <dn>את</dn> the voice of the bride. For the land shall become a waste!</dq>
[Jeremiah 8:1] <dq>“At that time,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“they shall bring <dn>את</dn> the bones of the sovereigns of Yehuḏah, and <dn>את</dn> the bones of its heads, and <dn>את</dn> the bones of the priests, and <dn>את</dn> the bones of the prophets, and <dn>את</dn> the bones of the inhabitants of Yerushalayim, out of their burial-sites,</dq>
[2] <dq>and shall spread them before the sun and the moon and all the host of the heavens, which they have loved and which they have served and after which they have walked, which they have sought, and to which they have bowed themselves. They shall not be gathered nor buried, they shall be for dung on the face of the earth.</dq>
[3] <dq>“And death shall be preferred to life by all the rest of those who remain of this evil people, who remain in all the places where <dn>I</dn> have driven them,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts.
